A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same confidence-ranking method and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. v3 retains Appendices A–E and adds Appendix F, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ranking-loss and AUROC experiments, cascade coverage and success rates, a Bernoulli simulation, and supplementary analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds AUROC sensitivity results and training-margin trajectories in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The confidence-estimator architecture, simulated-annotator features, margin-based objective, and alternating optimizer are unchanged. The added test-time feature explanation in Section 3.1 documents the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use AlpacaEval, HH-RLHF, Chatbot Arena, TL;DR, and the same Bernoulli simulation scenario. Appendix F reuses existing datasets and introduces no new task or domain.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4 retain the same confidence-estimator baselines and cascade comparisons. Appendix F introduces no new comparison method; the beta=0 condition already appears in Table 3.

E3.justification: The existing Mistral beta sweep gains AUROC evaluation in Table 5, complementing Table 3's ranking loss. Table 6 reports gamma at epochs 1, 10, 20, and 30. The beta grid, training budget, and original calibration and cascade settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 already contains beta sensitivity and training-loss convergence analyses in Table 3 and Figure 5. v3 extends these diagnostics with AUROC sensitivity and representative adaptive-margin trajectories for Mistral on Chatbot Arena and HH-RLHF.

E5.justification: Both retain the 1,000 random-split cascade evaluations and 10,000-trial simulation. Tables 5–6 add point results and a representative trajectory without new run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–5 retain their results. Table 5 adds AUROC values across beta settings, including 0.7156 for Chatbot Arena at beta=10^-3. Table 6 reports gamma increasing from 0.0109 to 0.0626 on Chatbot Arena and 0.0102 to 0.0253 on HH-RLHF between epochs 1 and 30.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, bounds, and proofs, including Appendices A–C, are unchanged. The added explanation that the standard ranking loss uses gamma=0 restates the existing definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: learned margin-adaptive confidence ranking, PAC-Bayesian generalization bounds, and empirical improvements in monotonicity and cascade guarantee success.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the margin trade-off, ranking generalization, monotonicity, and cascade reliability remain unchanged. Appendix F adds diagnostic observations without substantive new interpretations, applicability qualifications, or limitations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link in Section 5.2 and an AlpacaEval repository URL. Sections 2–3.1 clarify the distinction between annotation examples and test inputs and explain running the judge with each in-context subset to obtain test-time features.

R1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same research positioning. Reference edits update existing works, including the Badshah entry retaining arXiv:2503.08542 and Zhuo's code-evaluation citation changing to ICE-Score/EACL 2024.

P1.justification: v3 adds brief methodological clarifications, lightly edits optimizer prose, updates affiliations and bibliographic information, and appends Appendix F. The main section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Appendix F adds two compact tables. Existing Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–4 retain their displays, while added prose causes limited main-text reflow.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's ranking-loss sweep and convergence plot, v3 adds complementary AUROC sensitivity and actual margin trajectories, making adaptive training more transparent. Test-time feature clarifications and code-access information also improve reproducibility documentation. These are useful, limited gains; the main results, theory, and claims remain unchanged.
